Add transition-shadow duration-150 ease-out to each tab button, and do not use transition-all.
Build the stylesheet from the input file.
Write tests/tabs-focus.spec.ts that presses Tab to reach the first tab and expects its computed box-shadow not to be none.
Run the focus spec.
Run the accessibility checker against the tabs page.

K-021882.example: Pressing Tab moves focus to the first tab and its box-shadow ring appears over 150ms. A mouse click does not show the ring because focus-visible skips pointer focus.
K-021882.check: Playwright prints 1 passed and axe reports 0 color-contrast violations.
traps: Using focus: instead of focus-visible:, which shows a ring after every mouse click.
Removing the outline with no visible replacement, which leaves keyboard users without a focus indicator.
Setting transition-all, which animates every property including layout.

steps.do: Open the tab script to see how selection is handled.

Add an absolutely positioned span with classes pointer-events-none absolute left-0 top-0 rounded-md bg-slate-200 transition-[transform,width] duration-300 ease-in-out motion-reduce:transition-none, and give the tablist the class relative.
In src/tabs.js, on each selection set the pill's style transform to translateX of the tab's offsetLeft in px and its width to the tab's offsetWidth in px.
Call the same position update on window resize so the pill stays aligned.
Check the script's syntax.
Write tests/tabs-pill.spec.ts that expects the pill's computed transition-duration to be 0.3s and its transform to match the active tab's offsetLeft.
Run the pill spec.

K-021883.example: Selecting a tab at offsetLeft 240px moves the pill with transform translateX(240px) over 300ms. Under reduced motion the same move happens instantly because motion-reduce:transition-none applies.
K-021883.check: node --check exits 0 with no output, and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Animating left instead of transform, which forces layout work on every frame.
Forgetting the resize update, so the pill drifts out of alignment after the window changes size.
Setting transition-all on the tablist, which animates unrelated properties.

steps.do: Open the tab markup to find the tab buttons.
Give each tab button the classes transition-colors duration-150 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)] text-slate-500 hover:text-slate-900 aria-selected:text-indigo-600.
Add motion-reduce:transition-none to each tab button so reduced-motion users get instant color changes.
Build the stylesheet from the input file.
Confirm the 150ms duration was generated.
Confirm the cubic-bezier easing was generated.

K-021884.example: Clicking a tab changes its text from slate-500 to indigo-600 over 150ms along the cubic-bezier easing. The aria-selected attribute drives the color, so the visual state and the accessible state stay in sync.
K-021884.check: Both grep commands exit 0, and the output shows 150ms and cubic-bezier.
traps: Writing ease-cubic-bezier, which is not a real class; the arbitrary form is ease-[...].
Using selected: instead of aria-selected:, so the color never follows the accessible selected state.
Typing duration-1500 instead of duration-150, which makes the transition ten times slower.

steps.do: In tabs-plan.md, list the five tokens: --tab-fg, --tab-fg-selected, --tab-bg-selected, --tab-indicator, and --tab-focus-ring.
Write the minimum contrast beside each token: [REDACTED] for text tokens and 3:1 for --tab-indicator and --tab-focus-ring.
Count the token lines in the plan.
Confirm the plan states the 4.5:1 minimum.

K-021885.example: The plan writes --tab-fg-selected at 4.5:1 against its background in both themes. --tab-indicator and --tab-focus-ring each need 3:1 against the adjacent surface.
K-021885.check: The first grep prints 5 and the second prints 1 or more.
traps: A small model often sets the 4.5:1 rule only for text and forgets the 3:1 rule for the indicator and focus ring.
Each token needs a value for both themes, so a token with only a light value is incomplete.

steps.do: Locate the asset catalog that will hold the color tokens.
Record the primary text pair with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1.
Record secondary text, used only for 18-point or larger headers, with a ratio of at least 3 to 1.
Confirm the Swift toolchain is installed before any color check runs.
Confirm the sources folder exists where the token files will go.

K-021886.example: Primary label #1D1D1F on white is about 16.9:1, which passes 4.5 to 1. Light gray #AAAAAA on white is about 2.3:1, which fails and must not be used for row text.
K-021886.check: The contrast ratio is (L1 + 0.05) divided by (L2 + 0.05), and a passing pair prints 4.5 or higher; swift --version prints a line starting with Swift version.
traps: Judging contrast by eye instead of computing the ratio leads to light gray text that fails.
Applying the 3-to-1 large-text rule to body text fails the 4.5-to-1 requirement.

steps.do: Check whether the terminal exports COLORFGBG, which holds foreground and background color indexes.
Find any code that already reads COLORFGBG.
Plan to send the OSC 11 background query, which is ESC then ]11 then a question mark then BEL, and read the reply from the TTY.
Plan to parse the rgb reply, compute relative luminance, and choose dark below a mid-gray cutoff such as 0.5.
Set the fallback to dark when no reply arrives within 200ms.
Plan a --theme light and --theme dark override that skips detection.

K-021887.example: A reply of rgb:1e1e/1e1e/2e2e has low luminance, so the plan selects dark. A terminal that never answers the query falls back to dark after 200ms.
K-021887.check: The printf command prints the variable value, and a reply of the form rgb:RRRR/GGGG/BBBB parses to dark when its luminance is under the cutoff.
traps: Waiting forever for the OSC 11 reply hangs the app on terminals that ignore the query.
Reading COLORFGBG alone misses terminals that do not set it.

steps.do: Create the docs directory if it is missing.
Create the empty plan file.
Write the targets: body text at least 4.5:1 against the background, and UI borders and focus at least 3:1, for both dark and light themes.
Write the performance target: theme detection finishes within 200ms and the app starts in under 300ms.
Confirm the plan file is nonempty after you add the decisions.

K-021888.example: docs/theming-plan.md lists the dark text pair #cdd6f4 on #1e1e2e as the first contrast pair to test at 4.5:1 or higher. The build stage checks each pair with a script before merging.
K-021888.check: test -s docs/theming-plan.md exits 0, and the file lists a 4.5:1 text target and a 200ms detection limit.
traps: Writing targets as looks good gives the build stage nothing to measure.
Applying the 4.5:1 body text target to large UI elements makes the plan stricter than needed, while the 3:1 target is too loose for body text.

steps.do: List the CSS and HTML files that may hold tab styles or markup.
Count the hex color literals in each file.
Find every rgb or rgba literal so none is missed.
In tabs-plan.md, write one line per color with its selector and a proposed token name such as --tab-fg.
Confirm tabs-plan.md has at least 2 lines, one per color found in the scan.

K-021889.example: A tabs stylesheet sets 'color: #333' on .tab and 'background: #fff' on .tab[aria-selected=true], so the scan finds 2 hex colors in 1 file. The plan maps them to --tab-fg and --tab-bg-selected.
K-021889.check: rg -c prints a count of 2 for tabs.css, and wc -l prints a number of at least 2.
traps: A small model often misses rgb() and hsl() values because it only searches for hex codes.
Do not replace colors in this stage. The plan only names them.

steps.do: Check whether the project already sets the color-scheme property.
Check whether the project already uses the prefers-color-scheme media query.

Record in tabs-plan.md the decision: :root sets color-scheme: light dark, html[data-theme=dark] overrides the tokens, and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) supplies the default when no data-theme is set.
Confirm the plan names the data-theme attribute at least 2 times.

K-021890.example: The plan sets color-scheme: light dark on :root so native scrollbars and form controls follow the theme. A manual toggle writes data-theme=dark on the html element, and the media query applies only when that attribute is absent.
K-021890.check: grep -c prints 2 or more, and the plan contains the words prefers-color-scheme and color-scheme.
traps: A small model often forgets color-scheme, which leaves native controls in the wrong mode.
Do not write the toggle in this stage. Decide the mechanism only.

steps.do: List any existing files whose name starts with tabs, in any directory.
List the ui directory to see the current layout.
In tabs-plan.md, list the planned paths: ui/tabs/index.html, ui/tabs/tabs.css, ui/tabs/theme.css, and ui/tabs/tabs.js.
Confirm the plan lists exactly 4 planned paths under ui/tabs/.

K-021891.example: The search finds no existing tabs files under ui, so the planned paths are free. The plan then keeps the token file theme.css separate from the component file tabs.css.
K-021891.check: find prints no paths that would be overwritten, and grep -c prints 4 or more.
traps: A small model often creates files before checking names, which can overwrite a file the user already has.
Keep the token file separate from the component file so theme changes do not touch component layout.

steps.do: Find the head element where an inline script can run before the body paints.
Check whether the project already reads localStorage.
In tabs-plan.md, write the storage key tabs-theme with allowed values light, dark, and system.
Note in the plan that the inline script sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme and wraps the localStorage read in try and catch.
Confirm the storage key tabs-theme appears at least 1 time in the plan.

K-021892.example: An inline script in the head reads localStorage key tabs-theme and sets data-theme on the html element before the body paints. If localStorage throws in private browsing, the catch block leaves the default system value in place.
K-021892.check: rg finds the head element, and grep -c prints 1 or more for tabs-theme in the plan.
traps: A small model often places the script at the end of body, which causes a visible flash of the wrong theme.
Reading localStorage without try and catch can throw in some private modes and stop the script.

steps.do: Check whether a design tokens file already exists under Sources.
Create the docs folder for the token record.
Record spacing tokens in points: xs 4 (a half step), s 8, m 16, l 24, and a minimum table row height of 44 for touch targets. Every value except xs is a multiple of 8.
Check that the saved record contains row_min=44. The output must show line 1 with 44. If the 44-point minimum is missing, stop and fix the record.
Create the folder that will hold the token files.
Confirm the folder exists.

K-021893.example: No DesignTokens.swift exists, so the plan sets spacing to 4, 8, 16, and 24 points and row height to 44 points. The folder Sources/App/Theme is created to hold DesignTokens.swift.
K-021893.check: find prints nothing when no token file exists yet, grep prints line 1 containing row_min=44, and test -d exits with status 0 and no output.
traps: Choosing 40 points for rows misses the 44-point minimum.
A fixed .frame(height: 44) in a view is not a token; the value must be a named static let.

steps.do: Check whether a config directory already exists for the app.
Count the existing theme.toml files under the project. The count must be 0 before the build stage.
Pick the path ~/.config/myapp/theme.toml and list it in the plan.
Define exactly these eight keys: background, surface, text, muted, accent, success, warning, and error.

Specify that each key has a light value and a dark value, both as hex, plus an ANSI index fallback for 16-color terminals. Text on background must reach a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 in both the light and dark tables.

K-021894.example: The plan sets background to #1e1e2e under the dark table and #eff1f5 under the light table in theme.toml. The accent key lists ANSI index 4 as its 16-color fallback. The text-on-background pair is checked at 4.5:1 or higher in both tables.
K-021894.check: find . -name theme.toml prints no path, so the count is 0, and the plan lists exactly eight keys with a 4.5:1 minimum contrast for text on background.
traps: Naming keys after colors such as blue makes light and dark swaps confusing.
Storing a separate theme file per mode duplicates keys and lets them drift apart.

steps.do: Confirm the stylesheet has a prefers-reduced-motion media query.
Confirm the reduced-motion block sets transition-duration to 0.01ms or lower.
Run the Playwright test that emulates reduced motion and checks computed durations.

K-021895.example: styles/layout.css line 42 has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) with .drawer { transition-duration: 0.01ms; }. The spec calls page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }) and expects the computed transitionDuration of .drawer to be under 0.001s.
K-021895.check: grep prints line 42 and the Playwright run prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models often forget that emulateMedia must run before the page loads or the query is not applied.
Setting display: none in the reduced block is not the same as stopping motion, so check the duration value instead.

steps.do: Run Lighthouse on the built page and save the performance result as JSON.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the saved report.
Check that the value is 0.1 or lower, the good threshold for CLS.

K-021896.example: The page is served at localhost:8080 and the report is written to lh-layout.json. The jq command prints 0.02, which is below the 0.1 limit.
K-021896.check: jq prints a number at or below 0.1, such as 0.02.
traps: Small models often pass a width or top animation that still causes layout shift.
Lighthouse needs a running server, so start the local server before running it.

steps.do: List every transition-duration or animation-duration declaration with its line number.
Count the declarations to confirm the number matches the components you expect to animate.
Change any value outside 150ms to 300ms to the nearest bound, then rerun the first search.

K-021897.example: The first grep prints line 12 with transition-duration: 220ms and line 57 with transition-duration: 480ms. Line 57 is above 300ms, so it becomes 300ms.
K-021897.check: Every printed value is between 150ms and 300ms, and the count from the second grep equals the number of animated components.
traps: Small models often read 0.3s as a different value from 300ms, so convert before comparing.
Do not guess the range from memory, since the project may define its own limits in a CSS custom property.

steps.do: Confirm the timing test asserts a 200ms upper bound.
Run the drawer timing test with the line reporter.
If the test fails, read the measured elapsed time and reduce the transition duration in styles/layout.css.

K-021898.example: The spec opens .drawer and records performance.now() before and after the transitionend event. The measured value is 184ms, which passes toBeLessThan(200).
K-021898.check: grep prints the line with toBeLessThan(200) and the Playwright run prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models often time the click instead of the transitionend event, which measures the wrong interval.
Headless runs can also be faster than real devices, so the test shows the duration cap but not the device feel.

steps.do: Check whether a select component already exists in the source tree.
Confirm the installed Vue version in package.json.
Write the four states on paper: idle, loading, loaded, error.
Decide that the select is disabled and has aria-busy='true' while loading.
Set the budget that loading text appears within 200ms of the request starting.
Pick the file names src/components/BaseSelect.vue and src/components/BaseSelect.spec.ts.

K-021899.example: If package.json shows vue at 3.4 or later, the plan uses a ref<boolean> named isLoading with defineProps. The select gets disabled and aria-busy='true' while isLoading is true, and the list shows no BaseSelect.vue yet.
K-021899.check: rg prints no existing BaseSelect match, grep prints a line like '"vue": "^3.4.21"', and ls shows the components folder without BaseSelect.vue.
traps: A small model often plans only idle and loading and forgets the error state.
Do not plan the Options API with a data() object; use the Composition API with ref and computed.
Do not create the .vue file during the plan stage.

steps.do: Confirm the Vue test utilities package is listed in package.json.
Confirm the vitest version that will run the spec file.
Write test one: the select is disabled and aria-busy is true while loading.
Write test two: the select is enabled and shows the real options after loading finishes.
Write test three: an error sets the error text and clears the loading state.
Write test four: changing the select emits update:modelValue with the chosen value.

K-021900.example: The spec file has four cases, and each mounts BaseSelect with loading set to true or false. The run should show four passing tests with a time under 200ms per case.
K-021900.check: grep prints a line naming @vue/test-utils, and npx vitest --version prints a version number such as 2.1.0.
traps: A small model often writes only the happy-path test and skips the error case.
Do not mock the whole Vue runtime; mount the component with @vue/test-utils.
Do not plan tests that depend on a real network call, because they are slow and flaky.

steps.do: Confirm that eslint is installed so the accessibility rules can run later.
Check the existing style files for the color and size tokens in use.
Set the select height to at least 44px so it is a usable touch target.
Set the loading text color to reach a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background.
Plan a polite live region with aria-live='polite' that announces when loading finishes.

K-021901.example: The select gets min-height: 44px, and the loading text uses a color with a 4.5:1 contrast ratio on white. A div with aria-live='polite' announces 'Options loaded' after the request finishes.
K-021901.check: npx eslint --version prints a version number, rg lists the color tokens in the stylesheet, and the plan records the 44px and 4.5:1 numbers as written targets.
traps: A small model often picks a light gray text color that fails the 4.5:1 contrast rule.
Do not rely on a spinner alone; screen readers need text or aria-live to hear the loading state.
Do not set aria-live='assertive' for routine loading, because it interrupts the user.

steps.do: Create the charts folder.
Create the page file.
Write an svg with role='img' and aria-labelledby='t1 d1', then a title with id t1 and a desc with id d1 as its first children, followed by one rect per bar.
Start a local server in a second terminal so axe can load the page.
Count the title elements, expecting one.
Run axe against the page and expect zero violations.

K-021902.example: A bar chart of three values (12, 30, 7) uses title id t1 'Sales by region 2026' and desc id d1 'East 12, West 30, North 7'. The svg carries aria-labelledby='t1 d1' so a screen reader announces both.
K-021902.check: grep prints 1 and axe reports 'Violations found: 0'.
traps: Setting role='img' with no accessible name leaves the chart unlabeled for screen readers.
Keeping the summary only in visible text and skipping desc hides the data from assistive tech.
The aria-labelledby ids must match the title and desc ids exactly, including case.

steps.do: Create the table file.
Write a table with a caption element and a thead row whose th elements have scope='col', with no scope on body cells.
Add class sr-only to the table, and in charts/chart.css define .sr-only with position absolute, width 1px, height 1px, overflow hidden, and clip-path inset 50%.
Count the scope attributes, expecting one per column header.
Confirm the sr-only rule exists in the stylesheet.

K-021903.example: A table with caption 'Sales by region 2026' has headers Region, Units, Share, each with scope='col', and three body rows that match the three bars. Its class sr-only keeps it readable to assistive tech while hidden on screen.
K-021903.check: grep -c prints 3 and grep -n prints a line such as 12:.sr-only { position: absolute; ... }.
traps: Using display none removes the table from the accessibility tree, so screen readers skip it.
Leaving scope off the th cells makes screen readers lose the column association.
Using clip rather than clip-path leaves the old deprecated property in place.

steps.do: Create the stylesheet.
Set the bar fill to #949494, which gives 3.03:1 against white, and the axis label color to #767676, which gives 4.54:1 against white.
Check the fill attributes in the markup against the chosen hex values.
Run axe with only the color-contrast rule and expect zero violations on the text labels.

K-021904.example: Bars use fill #949494 on a white background (3.03:1, passes the 3:1 graphics rule), and tick labels use #767676 (4.54:1, passes the 4.5:1 text rule). Both colors come from the stated ratios, not from eye judgment.
K-021904.check: grep shows the fill hex values, and axe prints 'Violations found: 0' for color-contrast.
traps: Using the 3:1 graphics threshold for text labels, which need 4.5:1 instead.
Choosing light grey like #cccccc, which is about 1.6:1 against white and fails both thresholds.
Assuming axe checks SVG rect fills, which it does not, so compute the ratio by hand.

steps.do: Write a transition on .bar of height 300ms ease-out in charts/chart.css.
Add an @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block after that rule that sets transition none and animation none on .bar.
Create a Playwright spec that emulates reduced motion and reads the computed transition-duration of a bar.
Run the spec and expect it to pass.
Count the reduced-motion media queries, expecting one.

K-021905.example: Under reduce, the .bar transition is none, so computed transition-duration is 0s; under no-preference it reads 0.3s. The spec calls page.emulateMedia with reducedMotion set to reduce, then asserts 0s.
K-021905.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep -c prints 1.
traps: Putting the media query before the base .bar rule, so the base rule wins by source order.
Shortening the duration to 1ms instead of none, which still counts as motion for some users.
Skipping the emulateMedia call, so the test never triggers reduce and passes by accident.

steps.do: Give each rect a tabindex of 0 and an aria-label with its category and value.
Add a :focus-visible rule with outline 3px solid #005fcc and outline-offset 2px in charts/chart.css.
Count tabindex attributes in the markup, expecting one per bar.
Run Lighthouse with only the accessibility category and write the JSON report to stdout.

K-021906.example: Each of six rects has tabindex='0' and aria-label='East: 12 units', and the focus ring is 3px in #005fcc. The Lighthouse JSON reports the accessibility category score.
K-021906.check: grep -c prints 6 for six bars and the Lighthouse JSON shows an accessibility score of 1.
traps: Setting outline none with no replacement ring, which hides focus completely.
Setting tabindex above 0, which reorders the Tab sequence.
Putting focus only on the svg element, so individual bars cannot be reached.

steps.do: Confirm the stylesheet file exists before searching it.
Search for transitions on layout properties. This must print no lines.
Confirm transform or opacity drives the moving parts. This must print at least one line.
Print every millisecond duration in the stylesheet. Each number must be 300ms or less.
If step 2 printed any lines, locate those transition lines so you can change them to transform: translateX or translateY by hand.

K-021907.example: The first grep prints the path test passes on. The second grep prints nothing. The third grep prints line 18 with transition: transform 250ms ease-out. The fourth grep prints 250ms, which is under 300ms. A .sidebar that used left 300ms would have matched the second grep at its line number.
K-021907.check: Step 2 prints no lines, step 3 prints at least one line containing transform or opacity, and every number printed by step 4 is 300 or less.
traps: Small models often search for transition: all, which hides the real properties.
A grep with no output is only a pass when the file path is correct, so confirm the file exists first.

steps.do: Wait 500ms so the 250ms entrance animation has finished.
Run axe against the settled page.
In the same shell session, print the exit code from the previous axe run. It must print 0, which means no violations were found.
If axe reported a violation, list the color rules in the stylesheets to find the color of the element that moved.
After raising the text color to at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background for normal text, rerun axe on the settled page.

K-021908.example: The page at localhost:8080 finishes its slide-in in about 250ms. The wait step covers 500ms, then axe reports zero violations and echo prints 0. A failed run would list the rule id and the affected selector.
K-021908.check: The axe output ends with zero violations, and the echo step prints 0, which is the exit code of the axe run.
traps: Small models often run axe while the animation is still moving, which can flag transient states.
Wait until the transition has ended before running the check.

steps.do: Find existing v-model bindings to copy the naming pattern.
Check that TypeScript strict mode is enabled.
Write the props type with modelValue as string or null, options as an array of objects with value and label, and loading as an optional boolean.
Write the emits type with one event named update:modelValue that carries a string or null.
Set the default for loading to false using withDefaults.
Count the files that already use defineProps so you can compare the new file against them.
Run the type checker after the props and emits are written; expect exit code 0 and zero errors.

K-021909.example: The props are modelValue: string | null, options: { value: string; label: string }[], and loading: boolean with a default of false. The only emit is 'update:modelValue', so the parent can use v-model on BaseSelect.
K-021909.check: rg prints the existing v-model lines, grep shows 'strict': true, rg -c prints a count of files that use defineProps, and npx vue-tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 and zero errors.
traps: A small model often types modelValue as string only and forgets null for the empty choice.
Do not use a prop named value, because v-model on a component expects modelValue in Vue 3.
Do not add a loading prop as required; keep it optional so existing parents still compile.

steps.do: Search for existing fetch calls to see how the project loads data.
Check whether vitest is installed to test the request flow later.
Decide that the parent owns the request and passes loading as a prop to BaseSelect.
Plan that isLoading is set to true before the request and false in a finally block.
Run vitest on the request flow test; expect exit code 0 and exactly 1 request per mount.
Confirm the fetch endpoint is a single URL string and not built from user input.

K-021910.example: The parent page calls fetch('/api/regions') once in onMounted, sets isLoading to true first, and clears it in finally. BaseSelect only renders the state it receives.
K-021910.check: rg lists the fetch calls in the project, grep returns a vitest line if the test runner exists, and npx vitest run exits with code 0 while the request count per mount is 1.
traps: A small model often lets the select fetch and the parent fetch, which doubles the requests.
Do not clear the loading flag only in the success path; a failed request then leaves the select stuck in loading.
Do not use Suspense for this plan, because it is still experimental and needs an async setup function.

steps.do: Check how existing selects render option elements.
Check whether a loading message already exists in the source.
Plan one placeholder option with value set to an empty string and the disabled attribute set.
Set the placeholder text to 'Loading options...' and show it only when loading is true and options is empty.
Run the component test and expect exit code 0 with exactly 1 rendered option while loading, and 0 of those options enabled.

K-021911.example: While isLoading is true and options is an empty array, the select renders one option with value='' and the disabled attribute and the text 'Loading options...'. Once the data arrives, v-for replaces it with the real options.
K-021911.check: rg shows the existing option markup, and npx vitest run exits with code 0 while the rendered option count is 1 and the enabled option count is 0.
traps: A small model often leaves the placeholder selectable, so the user can pick an empty value by mistake.
Do not render the placeholder when options already has items, because it hides the real choices.
Do not use a select element with no options at all; screen readers announce it as empty.

steps.do: Create lib/widgets/city_autocomplete.dart with a ValueNotifier<bool> named isLoading that starts as false.
In optionsBuilder, return const Iterable<String>.empty() when textEditingValue.text has fewer than 2 characters, and otherwise set isLoading.value to true before the fetch.
Use optionsViewBuilder to place a LinearProgressIndicator with minHeight 2 at the top of the options Material when isLoading is true.
Make each option ListTile at least 48 pixels tall by wrapping it in a ConstrainedBox with minHeight 48.
Write test/widgets/city_autocomplete_test.dart that types 'Be' and expects find.byType(LinearProgressIndicator) to findsOneWidget before the fake future completes.
Run the analyzer on the file to catch unused imports and type errors.

K-021912.example: Typing 'Be' sets isLoading to true, so a 2-pixel LinearProgressIndicator appears above the list until the fake fetch completes after 500ms. The test uses a Completer so the spinner can be checked before the future resolves.
K-021912.check: The test command prints '+1: All tests passed!' and flutter analyze prints 'No issues found!'.
traps: Small models set isLoading true but never set it back to false when the fetch fails, so the bar stays forever.
Returning null from optionsBuilder instead of an empty Iterable causes a type error.
Forgetting that Autocomplete rebuilds options on every keystroke, so each keystroke can start a new fetch without cancelling the old one.

steps.do: List every millisecond duration in the chart bar component.
Open the Playwright config to confirm the base URL and projects.
Run the bar transition timing spec.
Confirm the run reports zero failed tests and the measured transition is 300ms or less.

K-021946.example: ChartBar.vue sets transition: height 240ms ease-out on .bar. The spec measures 240ms from transitionstart to transitionend and passes against the 300ms limit.
K-021946.check: Playwright output ends with '1 passed' and the expect(duration).toBeLessThanOrEqual(300) assertion passes.
traps: Small models check the CSS value with grep but never measure runtime timing. A grep match proves the value exists, not that it runs at that speed.

steps.do: Find every reduced motion media query in the source tree.
Open the reduced motion spec to see what it checks.
Run the reduced motion spec on the chromium project.
Confirm the computed transition-duration on .bar is 0s when reduced motion is emulated.

K-021947.example: The spec calls page.emulateMedia with reducedMotion set to reduce, then reads getComputedStyle on .bar and expects transitionDuration to equal 0s. The CSS block @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) sets .bar { transition: none }.
K-021947.check: Output shows '1 passed' and the computed transition-duration equals 0s in the spec log.

steps.do: Confirm the legend uses TransitionGroup with a name and a move class.
Run the legend unit spec with vitest.
Lint the legend component with the Vue plugin rules.
Confirm the vitest run reports 3 passed tests and eslint reports no errors.

K-021948.example: ChartLegend.vue wraps items in <TransitionGroup name='legend'> with .legend-move { transition: transform 200ms }. The spec mounts 3 items, reorders them, and asserts the legend-move class is applied.
K-021948.check: vitest prints 'Tests 3 passed' and eslint prints no output with exit code 0.

steps.do: Find every requestAnimationFrame call in the chart components.
Run the frame rate spec that counts animation frames over one second.
Confirm the spec reports at least 50 frames in 1000ms and an average gap under 20ms.

K-021949.example: The spec triggers a bar animation, runs a rAF counter for 1000ms, and records 58 frames. It asserts frames is at least 50, which is 50fps or better.
K-021949.check: Playwright output shows '1 passed' and the logged frame count is 50 or higher.
traps: Small models measure with console.time around the trigger call, not across the frames. That measures JS setup time, not animation smoothness.
Headless runs can cap frame rate differently from real hardware. State that the number comes from headless Chromium in the report.

steps.do: Build the production bundle so Lighthouse tests the real output.
Create the reports folder for Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse performance audit on the dashboard page.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the Lighthouse JSON.

K-021950.example: The dashboard with animated bars reports a cumulative-layout-shift numericValue of 0.02. That is below the 0.1 limit, so the animation causes no visible jump.
K-021950.check: jq prints a number below 0.1 for cumulative-layout-shift.
traps: Small models run Lighthouse against the dev server, which has different timing and bundle size. Use the built output served on port 4173.
A high CLS often comes from animating width or height instead of transform. Check the CSS property before raising the limit.

steps.do: Find the frame loop start and cleanup calls in the chart component.
Run the unmount spec with vitest.
Lint the chart component to catch missing cleanup patterns.
Confirm vitest reports 1 passed and cancelAnimationFrame was called once per started loop.

K-021951.example: ChartBar.vue starts the loop in onMounted and calls cancelAnimationFrame(frameId) in onBeforeUnmount. The spec spies on window.cancelAnimationFrame, unmounts the wrapper, and expects exactly 1 call.
K-021951.check: vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed' and the spy call count is 1.
traps: Small models often verify the animation runs but skip the unmount path. A leaked loop keeps running after the chart is gone.
Calling cancelAnimationFrame with the wrong frame id, or not storing the id, stops nothing. Store the id returned by requestAnimationFrame in a variable.

steps.do: List every token name used in onboarding.tcss.
List every token name defined in tokens.tcss.
Run the token test that fails on any undefined name.

K-021952.example: onboarding.tcss uses $text-muted and $accent, and tokens.tcss defines both, so the test prints 2 passed. If $accent were missing from tokens.tcss, the test would fail with a message naming $accent.
K-021952.check: The pytest line ends with 'N passed' and 0 failed, and every name from the first rg list appears in the second.

Do not add a token to onboarding.tcss without defining it in tokens.tcss first. Textual silently ignores unknown variables, so the failure shows up only at runtime.

steps.do: Run the contrast test for text tokens against surface tokens.
Confirm the test sets 4.5 as the minimum ratio.
Rerun the contrast test with verbose output to see each pair measured.

K-021953.example: #767676 on #ffffff measures 4.54:1 and passes, while #808080 on #ffffff measures 3.95:1 and fails. The test prints 1 passed when every pair is at or above 4.5:1.
K-021953.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the rg step shows the 4.5 threshold line.
traps: Do not treat 4.5:1 as the target for large or bold headings. Use the same threshold unless the test file says otherwise.
Do not estimate the contrast by eye. Only the measured ratio from the test counts as proof.

steps.do: Search onboarding.tcss for six-digit hex color literals.
Search the onboarding Python files for hex literals too.
Run the test that fails on any hex literal outside tokens.tcss.

K-021954.example: If onboarding.tcss contains 'color: #ff5555;', the first rg step prints that line with its line number. After the fix it uses 'color: $error;' and rg exits with code 1 and no output.
K-021954.check: Both rg steps print nothing and exit with code 1, and pytest ends with '1 passed'.
traps: rg exit code 1 with no output means zero matches. A small model may read the silence as an error and skip the step.
Do not count three-digit hex like #fff as safe. The regex above only checks six digits, so also search for '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3}'.

steps.do: Confirm the layout test runs the app at 80 columns by 24 rows.
Run the layout test headless at that size.
Run the layout test again with verbose output to see the widget sizes asserted.

K-021955.check: rg prints the size line, and pytest ends with '1 passed' with no clipping warnings.

A passing layout test does not prove the text is readable. Pair it with the contrast check for the same screen.

steps.do: Run the timing test that measures the time to mount the onboarding screen.
Confirm the test asserts the 200 millisecond limit.
Rerun the timing test with verbose output to see the measured time.

K-021956.example: The test wraps app.run_test() in time.perf_counter() and asserts elapsed < 0.200. A warm run that measures 143 ms prints '1 passed', while a 260 ms run fails with the measured value in the message.
K-021956.check: pytest ends with '1 passed', and the printed elapsed time is below 0.200 seconds.
traps: A small model may time a cold first run and treat its slowness as a failure. Run the test at least twice and compare the warm run.
Do not compare a time from a different machine. The 200ms limit applies only to the machine where the test runs.

Show the current content globs in the Tailwind config.

Confirm the planned class string appears in the plan file.

Show the #title selector block in onboarding.tcss.

K-021966.check: The first grep prints a line containing width: 60, and the second grep -c prints 0.

steps.do: Search the source for the wrap-around rule in the tab handler, to see whether the app wraps or stops at the last tab.
In tests/test_tabs_perf.py, press right twenty times in a loop with pilot.press, with no pause between presses.

Assert the total loop time is under 0.500 seconds.
Assert the final active index equals 2 when there are six tabs and the app wraps, because 20 mod 6 is 2. Tab indexes start at 0, so do not count from 1.

K-021968.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and the final index assertion matches the expected value.

steps.do: Search the source for forced layout refreshes in the tabs package.
Open the handler file from the search and find the refresh call that uses layout=True on the tab handler.
Change that call so it refreshes only the widget that changed, and remove only the forced full-layout flag. Keep the widget refresh, because it is needed for correctness.
Run the switch latency test and confirm the measured switch time is under 200ms.
Count the remaining forced layout calls per file in src/tabs_app, which must be zero for every file.

K-021969.example: The search finds layout=True in src/tabs_app/main.py on the tab handler, so the model changes it to refresh only the Tabs widget. After the change, grep -rc prints src/tabs_app/main.py:0 and the latency test passes.
K-021969.check: grep -rc reports 0 for every file in src/tabs_app, and pytest prints '1 passed' with the switch time under 200ms.
traps: Small models delete a refresh call that is needed for correctness. Remove only the forced full-layout flag, and keep the widget refresh.
Do not assume zero matches means the timing is fixed. Always rerun the latency test.

Count the test_ lines in PLAN.md.

Confirm pytest is installed for the build stage.

Confirm the utility classes made it into the compiled CSS.
Run the bar spec, which asserts transition-duration is 500ms and the bar reaches its target height.

K-021971.check: rg prints the origin-bottom line from dist/app.css, and playwright prints '1 passed' with no failed assertions.

Do not use transition-all, which animates unrelated properties.

Start the path hidden with the arbitrary properties [stroke-dasharray:1] and [stroke-dashoffset:1].

Find every chart path that has pathLength set.

The spec waits 900ms and expects computed stroke-dashoffset of 0.
K-021972.check: rg lists each chart path that has pathLength, and playwright prints '1 passed' with the offset assertion reading 0.

K-021973.check: rg prints each tooltip line with group-hover:opacity-100, and playwright prints '1 passed' with computed opacity 1.

Run the Playwright project that emulates reduced motion and reads transition-duration.

K-021974.check: The final rg -L prints no file names, and the playwright run prints '1 passed' with transitionDuration 0s for each element.
